solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Way to capture foreign part of fortification

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so the word for way takes the other piece within it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
alien means foreign, from another country

explanation.surface: An army's route is designed to seize an outlying portion of an enemy stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: In military architecture this is a projecting angle of a rampart or bastion, pointing outward toward attackers.

clue.text: Her music so confused a section of the choir

indicators.note: confused means jumbled up, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer complains that her piece of music has left part of the choir bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-chorus is a smaller group of singers drawn from the full choir, so it is one division of it.

clue.text: State of oblivion of bishop in posh car

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for bishop inside the word for a posh car

parts.note: a limo, short for limousine, is a luxurious car
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop forgotten in the back of a limousine is left in a state of neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo means being in an uncertain, neglected or forgotten condition, a kind of oblivion.

clue.text: Acquit former partner on single charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the former partner comes first

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
single means one
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A court clears someone's ex-spouse when only one count is brought against them.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit someone is to clear them of blame, which is to free them formally from a charge.

clue.text: Calamitous stunt mostly taking in a guide leader

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the shortened stunt word surrounds the next pieces
mostly means not quite all, so the stunt word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trick is a stunt or feat

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A daredevil's act mostly goes wrong after involving a Girl Guide leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TRICK to TRIC; 'taking in' puts A and G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragic is disastrous or catastrophic, a synonym for a calamitous event.

clue.text: Pith helmet — most superior one

parts.note: top means highest, most superior
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A colonial explorer's sun hat is declared the finest of them all.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi, or topee, is a lightweight sun hat made of pith, worn in hot countries in the colonial era.

clue.text: Tie-on label cheers granny at first

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, as is cheers

indicators.note: at first means take only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A gift label attached with string says thank you to Grandma first of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a small label attached to something, often tied on with string.

clue.text: Dad's pin-up eating top of raw vegetable

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the first pieces surround the next letter

parts.note: pa is dad, so Dad's gives PA'S

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
in a down clue, up means the word pin is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Father's pin-up poster is chewing on a raw root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pin-up' looks like one word, a poster; split, 'up' reverses PIN in this down clue, and 'eating' closes the father pieces round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Quiet member of the family?

definitions.meaning: keeping ... means saying nothing, staying silent
a mother is one of the family, informally called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is a friendly, familiar name rather than a formal description.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent as in keep mum, and the British informal word for mother, a relative in the household.

clue.text: Park-keeper visiting old Yankee where fruit-trees grow

indicators.note: visiting means going inside, so the keeper goes within the other two letters

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a ranger looks after a park or forest

explanation.surface: A park warden calls on an elderly American at a place where fruit trees are grown.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glass-walled building where orange and other citrus trees are cultivated.

clue.text: Lived it up, being famous

definitions.meaning: to live it up is to party and enjoy oneself, i.e. to have marked an occasion with festivities

explanation.surface: A celebrity is known for a party lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of marking an occasion with festivity and an adjective for renowned.

clue.text: Spice children initially think the world of

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word children

parts.note: to think the world of someone is to adore them

explanation.surface: Youngsters at first adore a particular seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove is the dried flower bud of a tropical tree used as a fragrant kitchen seasoning.

clue.text: Substance burnt in church? Not something evangelicals initiated!

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: initiated is read as giving the initial letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Fragrant smoke rises in a church service, though evangelical Christians would never introduce it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiated' takes N, S, E from 'Not something evangelicals'. The surface is apt: low-church evangelicals avoid incense.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is aromatic resin or gum burnt for its perfumed smoke, especially in religious rites.

clue.text: Boat made by Russian woman in prison

indicators.note: in places the woman's name inside the word for prison

parts.note: the can is American slang for jail
Tamara is a common Russian female name

explanation.surface: A vessel built by a Russian woman while she was serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a sailing vessel with two parallel hulls.

clue.text: Cost of old-fashioned ballad

parts.note: out means out of fashion, outdated
a lay is a narrative poem or song, a ballad

explanation.surface: Someone asks the price of a dated folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money spent, the expenditure or price of something.

clue.text: First-class food garnish

definitions.meaning: a layer such as cream, cheese or sauce put on top of a dish

explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for excellent, and the layer spread or sprinkled over a dish such as a pizza.

clue.text: Sound process identifying Russian plain

indicators.note: sound means the word said aloud, a homophone of the process word

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process, here taken as a process

explanation.surface: A reliable method is found for recognising a feature of Russian geography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective (reliable) but signals a homophone: the grassland word is pronounced like 'step'.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppe is the vast treeless grassland stretching across southern Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Worker on edge in Ulster county

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the worker comes first

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's classic worker insect
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A labourer is on a knife-edge somewhere in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, part of the historic province of Ulster, on its north-east coast.

clue.text: A great many put me out — active men, ultimately

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters of these two words are rearranged
ultimately means take the last letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone complains that lots of energetic men have finally ejected them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUTME into UMPTE; 'ultimately' adds E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is informal for an indefinitely large number, lots and lots.

clue.text: Big house in local police area

definitions.meaning: a large country house with its estate
British police slang for the district an officer covers, their patch

explanation.definitionFit: A grand country residence of a lord, and British police slang for an officer's home patch or beat.

clue.text: Simpleton's lodging-place in US city

indicators.note: in places the lodging word inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York
an inn offers lodging to travellers

explanation.surface: A fool's hotel room is in a big American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninny is a foolish or silly person, an idiot.

clue.text: Dreadful resistance restricting the indecisive type

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the first pieces enclose the following word

parts.note: dire means dreadful
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Awful opposition is holding back someone who cannot make up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like part of the definition but its letters are the ones enclosed by DIRE+R.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditherer hesitates and cannot make decisions, the wavering sort of person.

clue.text: Brick carrier finally buried under house

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so the house abbreviation comes first
finally means take the last letter of the word buried

explanation.surface: A builder's trough ends up interred beneath a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hod is an open box on a long pole used by builders to carry bricks over the shoulder.

clue.text: Ultimate feature of tennis court?

definitions.meaning: final after all deductions, as in a final result
the mesh barrier strung across the middle of the court

explanation.definitionFit: The word means final after all deductions, as in a bottom-line result, and names the mesh across a court's middle.

clue.text: Very old French painter returning without son

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the son letter is removed
returning means going back, so the painter's name is read backwards

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly French artist goes home without his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns DEGAS into SAGED; 'without' removes S.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, having lived a long time.

clue.text: Wealthy duke associated with circle in Yemen somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A rich aristocrat is linked with some ring of associates in Yemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The duke's D is not part of the rearranged letters: it sits at the end, after the shuffled O and YEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means having plenty of money, rich.
